q2_gaps: Ordinal day-of-year dating in a non-Gregorian calendar ("on day 100 of Year 1"): the Time section defines (Day <n>) as the calendar day inside a Month, and gives no convention for a bare day-number of a year, so (Day 100) is indistinguishable from a day-of-month and has no Month term for the seeded date-ordering rules to anchor on.

A bare MASS-noun argument of a specific episodic clause ("burned mire-essence", "contained salt-bloom", "produced mist-light") that is later re-mentioned as a definite ("The mire-essence in the lantern", "The mist-light"): the instruction set decides bare PLURALS (episodic -> group witness, generic -> kind) and reserves the bare class symbol for non-specific/generic objects, but says nothing about a bare mass noun that must later serve as a definite antecedent, so witness-vs-bare-kind is undetermined.
notes: The two parallel bare-mass objects are encoded differently - mire-essence as a witness (sk_mire_essence_1) but salt-bloom and sea-water as bare kind constants - which is internally inconsistent, though each choice is defensible on its own under the gap above. (PartOf sk_lantern_1 harbor_station) for "the lantern of the Harbor Station" turns on the part/component test and would equally support the opaque Possession fallback.
